summary: Two saved-study selections are resolved by the first completed read, so an earlier choice can silently discard the learner's latest choice.
fix: Reserve a selection-request generation when the history message is accepted, before readStudy starts; show the loading state immediately and apply only the latest requested study after I/O. Keep the displayed revision check for incoming stale messages separate from the generation used to arbitrate accepted pending selections.
evidence: receive(history) awaits "this.library!.readStudy(message.studyId)" (444) before any invalidation, then checks "message.revision !== this.revision" (445). The first completed read calls renderSelection, which increments revision at 317. Two valid messages A then B therefore share the old displayed revision: if A finishes first, B is discarded despite being the latest intent. A deferred-read harness executing the current transpiled receive method reproduced latestRequestedStudy=B, finalSelectedStudy=A, latestIntentPreserved=false. This occurs before source rendering and is distinct from the already reported renderSelection A-B-A race. Archives can contain tens of MiB, so the pending read is a real interaction boundary.
test_stub: test('the latest saved-study choice wins even when the earlier read finishes first', async () => { /* Arrange two deferred archive reads and one current displayed revision. */ const first = receiveHistory(studyA); const latest = receiveHistory(studyB); readA.resolve(archiveA); await first; readB.resolve(archiveB); await latest; assert.equal(reader.inspect().view.model.selection.studyId, studyB); assert.equal(renderedSourceHash, archiveB.observations[0].source.hash); });

summary: Selection from moments, source-linked flow, or Follow current never updates the native learning outline selection, leaving two different selected items visible.
fix: Synchronize the visible outline to the committed model participant using TreeView.reveal with select:true and focus:false, provide getParent for the flat roots, and synchronize on visibility when the outline is hidden so background updates do not unexpectedly open it. Cover flow/moment selection and automatic current-pause changes without stealing keyboard focus.
evidence: select updates "this.selection = { ...this.selection, participant: ..., follow: false }" (189), and refresh changes participant for Follow current (262). publish only assigns "this.outline.message" and invokes "this.treeChanges.fire(undefined)" (305-306). getTreeItem keeps stable item IDs (382), and there is no outline.reveal or other programmatic tree-selection operation anywhere in the implementation. Thus clicking Server in the native outline and then Browser in a webview changes the source/context model while retaining the native Server selection. Context7 official TreeView documentation and installed @types/vscode distinguish readonly selection/programmatic reveal from the tree-data refresh event. This is source/API evidence, not a claim of native pixel verification, and differs from the existing closed-outline progress refresh finding.
test_stub: test('selecting the browser moment synchronizes the native outline without moving focus', async () => { /* Arrange visible outline selected on server and focus in the moments webview. */ await dispatchReaderMessage({ type: 'select', revision: currentRevision, participant: 'browser' }); await settledReader; assert.deepEqual(tree.selection, ['browser']); assert.equal(reader.inspect().view.model.selection.participant, 'browser'); assert.equal(focusedRegion, 'moments'); });
